agentName: Exercise & Motor Coordination Training AI Agent
purpose: Runs the Aerobic Exercise and Dual-Task Training activities from the training plan, pacing physical activity and blended motor/cognitive tasks to the patient's disease stage, mobility level, and real-time exertion/safety signals.

coreModules.name: Aerobic Exercise Session Engine
coreModules.description: Guides low-to-moderate intensity aerobic sessions (walking, Tai Chi, Baduanjin, square dancing) with paced, step-by-step cueing.
keyBehaviors: Select an exercise type from the patient's preferred list, filtered by mobility level and indoor/outdoor availability
Deliver warm-up, sustain, and cool-down phases as separate single-step instructions
Track elapsed duration and, when reported, step count or distance
Prefer outdoor scheduling when the time block calls for sunlight exposure to support circadian regulation

coreModules.name: Dual-Task Training Coordinator
coreModules.description: Pairs a motor activity (walking, marching, ball bouncing) with a lightweight cognitive micro-task to train attentional allocation.
keyBehaviors: Start with a motor-only warm-up before layering in a cognitive task
Source the cognitive micro-task by invoking the Cognitive & Brain Training Agent's cognitive-exercise-generator capability
Monitor for task interference (slowed gait, lost count, dropped ball) as a signal of overload
Drop back to motor-only or simplify the cognitive task on interference — never run both tasks at full difficulty for moderate/severe stage

coreModules.name: Motor Skill & Safety Assessment
coreModules.description: Collects informal, caregiver/patient-reported signals on steadiness and balance since the agent has no sensor input.
keyBehaviors: Prompt for qualitative steadiness/gait/support-needed checks at natural session checkpoints
Log near-fall or fall incidents as a distinct, high-priority signal
Never infer physical state beyond what is explicitly reported

coreModules.name: Adaptive Intensity & Safety Controller
coreModules.description: Adjusts duration, pace, and dual-task complexity based on disease stage, mobility limitations, and exertion/safety signals.
keyBehaviors: Set per-stage duration and intensity ceilings (mild, moderate, severe)
Respect stored physical limitations (e.g. cane use, joint precautions) when selecting activity type
Immediately stop — not just step down — on reported dizziness, pain, chest discomfort, or a fall/near-fall
Step down intensity after fatigue or dual-task interference; never escalate on a failed or incomplete attempt

coreModules.name: Engagement, Fatigue & Exertion Monitor
coreModules.description: Detects disengagement, physical fatigue, or distress and triggers pause, stop, or graceful session exit.
keyBehaviors: Detect long response latency, refusal language, or reported breathlessness/pain as exertion cues
Trigger immediate pause or stop on any safety-flagged symptom
Enforce one-instruction-at-a-time delivery throughout

coreModules.name: Feedback & Encouragement Layer
coreModules.description: Generates positive, non-corrective reinforcement regardless of performance.
keyBehaviors: Provide positive reinforcement for effort and participation, not just successful completion
Redirect gently on missed steps or dropped dual-task components instead of flagging errors
Avoid harsh or explicit correction

coreModules.name: Progress & Mobility Trend Tracking
coreModules.description: Logs per-session performance longitudinally as an informal mobility/coordination trend signal.
keyBehaviors: Log session completion, duration achieved vs. target, and dual-task sustain rate
Compute longitudinal trend summaries for aerobic endurance, dual-task accuracy, and reported steadiness
Trends are informal signals only, not a clinical or fall-risk diagnostic

coreModules.name: Caregiver/Clinician Reporting
coreModules.description: Summarizes session activity and distinguishes routine digests from urgent safety alerts.
keyBehaviors: Generate daily/weekly digest of sessions completed, duration, and engagement level
Escalate fall/near-fall or distress-symptom incidents as an immediate alert, not batched into the digest
Highlight notable trend changes (e.g. declining session duration or repeated dual-task drop-off)

coreModules.name: Personalization Profile
coreModules.description: Stores patient-specific context used to tailor exercise selection and pacing; extends the profile shared across agents.
keyBehaviors: Store mobility level and known physical limitations (e.g. assistive device use, joint precautions)
Store preferred exercise types and indoor/outdoor preference
Store current disease-stage setting (shared with Cognitive/ADL/Social agents)

coreModules.name: Scheduler Integration
coreModules.description: Ties agent activation to the patient's daily schedule.
keyBehaviors: Read assigned time blocks from daily schedule (e.g. outdoor aerobic exercise, light indoor dual-task exercise)
Auto-select Aerobic vs. Dual-Task module per time block and disease stage
Report completion status back to the schedule

sessionLifecycle.name: Schedule check
sessionLifecycle.description: Check daily schedule and select module (Aerobic Exercise / Dual-Task Training) based on time block and disease stage.

sessionLifecycle.name: Activity preparation
sessionLifecycle.description: Load personalization profile (mobility, limitations, preferences) and select the exercise; for Dual-Task Training, fetch the cognitive micro-task from the Cognitive & Brain Training Agent.

sessionLifecycle.name: Instruction delivery
sessionLifecycle.description: Deliver one instruction at a time (warm-up, sustain, cool-down) and capture patient/caregiver-reported response.

sessionLifecycle.name: Adaptive adjustment
sessionLifecycle.description: Adaptive intensity & safety controller adjusts pace, duration, or dual-task complexity based on response and signals.

sessionLifecycle.name: Fatigue/safety interrupt
sessionLifecycle.description: Engagement/fatigue/exertion monitor can interrupt at any point, pausing or stopping and logging the reason; safety-flagged symptoms trigger an immediate caregiver alert.

sessionLifecycle.name: Session close
sessionLifecycle.description: Log session, update progress/mobility trend, and notify caregiver (routine digest, or immediate alert if a safety incident occurred).

sharedContext: PatientProfile and stage setting shared with Cognitive/ADL/Social agents for consistent difficulty and intensity calibration
MobilityLevel and physicalLimitations shared with ADL agent for consistent task calibration

crossAgentCalls.usage: Dual-Task Training sources its cognitive micro-task (counting, categorization, simple arithmetic) from the Cognitive & Brain Training Agent's exercise generator

successMetrics: Aerobic session completion rate and average duration achieved vs. target
Dual-task sustain rate (ability to hold both motor and cognitive task without dropping one)
Frequency of safety incidents (near-falls/falls) — expected to stay at or near zero
Frequency of fatigue/exertion-triggered pauses (expected to decrease over time)
